ei.title: 개인적 경험의 틀을 벗어나 다양한 관점으로 공감하기
ei.subject: 수능특강Light

fullPassage: We are all biased by our personal history. Our ingrained beliefs are the result of our personal experiences in the past, and they shape our visual prism. If you were born in a poor family or have been discriminated against, you already believe in something that people who have not experienced those things never will. You likely also grossly overestimate the chance of those events happening again. Morgan Housel offers a helpful suggestion to help us better empathize: “Start with the assumption that everyone is innocently out of touch and you’ll be more likely to explore what’s going on through multiple points of view, instead of cramming what’s going on into the framework of your own experiences. It’s hard to do. It’s uncomfortable when you do. But it’s the only way to get closer to figuring out why people behave like they do.”

questions.passage: We are all biased by our personal history. Our ingrained beliefs are the result of our personal experiences in the past, and they shape our visual prism. If you were born in a poor family or have been discriminated against, you already believe in something that people who have not experienced those things never will. You likely also grossly (A)[underestimate / overestimate] the chance of those events happening again. Morgan Housel offers a (B)[useless / helpful] suggestion to help us better empathize: “Start with the assumption that everyone is innocently out of touch and you’ll be more likely to explore what’s going on through multiple points of view, instead of cramming what’s going on into the framework of your own experiences. It’s hard to do. It’s (C)[uncomfortable / comfortable] when you do. But it’s the only way to get closer to figuring out why people behave like they do.”
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② overestimate — helpful — uncomfortable

(A) overestimate(과대평가하다): 가난·차별 같은 일을 겪은 사람은 그 일이 다시 일어날 가능성을 심하게 '과대평가'한다는 맥락이에요. underestimate(과소평가하다)는 편향의 방향과 반대예요.

(B) helpful(도움이 되는): Housel은 우리가 더 잘 공감하도록 '도움이 되는' 제안을 내놓아요. useless(쓸모없는)는 뒤의 to help us better empathize와 모순이에요.

(C) uncomfortable(불편한): 바로 앞 문장 It’s hard to do(하기 어렵다)와 이어지므로 '불편하다'가 자연스러워요. comfortable(편안한)은 흐름과 반대예요.
det.tip: overestimate ↔ underestimate, helpful ↔ useless, uncomfortable ↔ comfortable — 접두사·반의 관계로 문맥 방향을 확인하세요.

questions.passage: We are all biased by our personal history. Our (A)[temporary / ingrained] beliefs are the result of our personal experiences in the past, and they shape our visual prism. If you were born in a (B)[noble / poor] family or have been discriminated against, you already believe in something that people who have not experienced those things never will. You likely also grossly overestimate the chance of those events happening again. Morgan Housel offers a helpful suggestion to help us better (C)[empathize / argue]: “Start with the assumption that everyone is innocently out of touch and you’ll be more likely to explore what’s going on through multiple points of view, instead of cramming what’s going on into the framework of your own experiences. It’s hard to do. It’s uncomfortable when you do. But it’s the only way to get closer to figuring out why people behave like they do.”
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① ingrained — poor — empathize

(A) ingrained(뿌리 깊은): 과거 경험의 산물로 우리의 시각을 형성하는 '뿌리 깊은' 믿음이라는 맥락이에요. temporary(일시적인)는 과거 경험이 쌓여 만들어졌다는 설명과 어울리지 않아요.

(B) poor(가난한): 차별을 받은 경험과 나란히 제시되는 불리한 환경이므로 '가난한' 가정이 자연스러워요. noble(귀족의)은 차별 경험과 짝을 이루지 못해요.

(C) empathize(공감하다): 다양한 관점으로 타인을 이해하자는 글의 결론과 연결되므로 '공감하다'가 맞아요. argue(언쟁하다)는 제안의 목적과 반대예요.
det.tip: ingrained: 뿌리 깊은, 몸에 밴 / empathize: 공감하다 (em- 안에 + pathos 감정)

questions.passage: We are all biased by our personal history. Our ingrained beliefs are the result of our personal experiences in the past, and they shape our visual prism. If you were born in a poor family or have been discriminated against, you already believe in something that people who have not experienced those things never will. You likely also (A)[barely / grossly] overestimate the chance of those events happening again. Morgan Housel offers a helpful suggestion to help us better empathize: “Start with the assumption that everyone is (B)[deliberately / innocently] out of touch and you’ll be more likely to explore what’s going on through multiple points of view, instead of (C)[cramming / releasing] what’s going on into the framework of your own experiences. It’s hard to do. It’s uncomfortable when you do. But it’s the only way to get closer to figuring out why people behave like they do.”
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ④ grossly — innocently — cramming

(A) grossly(심하게): 개인적 경험이 만든 편향은 그 일이 재발할 가능성을 '심하게' 과대평가하게 해요. barely(거의 ~않게)는 과대평가한다는 동사와 논리적으로 충돌해요.

(B) innocently(악의 없이): Housel 인용의 핵심은 사람들이 '악의 없이' 현실 감각이 어긋나 있다고 전제하라는 거예요. deliberately(고의로)는 그 전제와 정반대예요.

(C) cramming(욱여넣기): 다양한 관점으로 탐색하는 것의 나쁜 대안, 즉 자기 경험의 틀에 상황을 '욱여넣는' 행위예요. releasing(내보내기)은 '틀 안에 욱여넣다(into ~)'라는 방향과 논리적으로 어긋나 부적절해요.
det.tip: instead of ~ing: '~하는 대신' — instead of 뒤에는 글이 경계하는 행동이 와요.

questions.passage: We are all ①<u>biased</u> by our personal history. Our ingrained beliefs are the result of our personal experiences in the past, and they shape our visual prism. If you were born in a poor family or have been ②<u>discriminated</u> against, you already believe in something that people who have not experienced those things never will. You likely also grossly overestimate the chance of those events happening again. Morgan Housel offers a helpful suggestion to help us better empathize: “Start with the assumption that everyone is innocently out of touch and you’ll be more likely to ③<u>ignore</u> what’s going on through multiple points of view, instead of cramming what’s going on into the framework of your own experiences. It’s hard to do. It’s uncomfortable when you do. But it’s the only way to get closer to figuring out why people ④<u>behave</u> like they do.”
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① biased(편향된): 우리는 모두 개인사에 의해 편향되어 있다 — 적절해요.

✅ ② discriminated(차별받은): 가난과 나란히 제시된 불리한 경험 — 적절해요.

❌ ③ ignore(무시하다): 원문은 explore(탐색하다)예요. '모두가 악의 없이 어긋나 있다'는 가정에서 출발하면 여러 관점으로 상황을 '탐색'하게 된다는 흐름인데, '무시한다'는 정반대예요. ←정답

✅ ④ behave(행동하다): 사람들이 왜 그렇게 행동하는지 — 적절해요.
det.tip: explore(탐색하다) ↔ ignore(무시하다)

questions.passage: We are all biased by our personal ①<u>history</u>. Our ingrained beliefs are the result of our personal experiences in the past, and they shape our visual prism. You likely also grossly ②<u>overestimate</u> the chance of those events happening again. Morgan Housel offers a helpful ③<u>suggestion</u> to help us better empathize: “Start with the assumption that everyone is innocently out of touch and you’ll be more likely to explore what’s going on through multiple points of view, instead of cramming what’s going on into the framework of your own experiences. It’s hard to do. It’s ④<u>comfortable</u> when you do. But it’s the only way to get closer to figuring out why people behave like they do.”
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① history(이력): 개인적 이력에 의해 편향된다 — 적절해요.

✅ ② overestimate(과대평가하다): 겪은 일의 재발 가능성을 과대평가한다 — 적절해요.

✅ ③ suggestion(제안): Housel이 도움이 되는 제안을 내놓는다 — 적절해요.

❌ ④ comfortable(편안한): 원문은 uncomfortable(불편한)이에요. 바로 앞의 It’s hard to do(하기 어렵다)와 이어지는 양보의 흐름이므로 '편안하다'는 모순이에요. ←정답
det.tip: It’s hard to do. It’s uncomfortable ~: 어렵고 불편하지만 유일한 방법이라는 양보 → 결론 구조

Morgan Housel offers a helpful suggestion to help us better empathize: “Start with the assumption that everyone is innocently out of touch and you’ll be more likely to explore what’s going on through ③<u>limited</u> points of view, instead of cramming what’s going on into the framework of your own experiences. det.analysis:
✅ ① poor(가난한): 차별 경험과 나란히 제시된 불리한 환경 — 적절해요.

✅ ② grossly(심하게): 재발 가능성을 심하게 과대평가한다 — 적절해요.

❌ ③ limited(제한된): 원문은 multiple(다양한)이에요. 자기 경험의 틀에 욱여넣는 대신 '다양한' 관점으로 탐색하라는 제안이므로, '제한된' 관점은 글의 제안과 정반대예요. ←정답

✅ ④ hard(어려운): 그렇게 하기가 어렵다 — 적절해요.
det.tip: multiple points of view: 다양한 관점 (multiple ↔ limited/single)

det.analysis:

❌ ② compete(경쟁하다): 타인을 이해하자는 제안과 반대 방향이에요.

❌ ③ apologize(사과하다): 글에 사과의 맥락이 없어요.

❌ ④ negotiate(협상하다): 협상 상황이 아니에요.

❌ ③ permanent(영구적인): 오래간다는 점에서 오히려 가까운 의미예요.

❌ ④ stubborn(완고한): 쉽게 바뀌지 않는다는 점에서 가까운 의미예요.
det.tip: ingrained(뿌리 깊은) ↔ superficial(피상적인)

questions.passage:
(A) Our early experiences <u>shape</u> the way we see other people. Even one strong memory can change our judgment for years.

(B) The baker pressed the dough into the <u>shape</u> of a star. The children picked the cookie with the sharpest points.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)의 밑줄 친 shape의 문맥적 의미로 가장 적절하게 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ (A) 형성하다 — (B) 모양

(A) 초기 경험이 타인을 보는 방식을 '형성한다'는 동사 용법이에요. 본문의 they shape our visual prism과 같은 쓰임이에요.

(B) 반죽을 별 '모양'으로 눌렀다는 명사 용법이에요.

❌ ① 의미가 서로 뒤바뀌었어요.

❌ ② '다듬다/상태'는 두 문맥 모두에 맞지 않아요.

❌ ④ '상태/유형'은 두 문맥 모두에 맞지 않아요.
det.tip: shape: ① (동사) 형성하다, 만들다 ② (명사) 모양, 형태

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"a set of ideas, rules, or beliefs that you use as a basis for judging or deciding things"

det.korean: 생각이나 판단의 기초가 되는 관념·규칙의 체계 = framework(틀)
det.analysis:
✅ ② framework(틀, 체계): 판단·결정의 기초가 되는 생각의 틀이라는 정의와 일치해요. 본문의 the framework of your own experiences(자기 경험의 틀)에서 쓰였어요.

❌ ① obstacle(장애물): 방해가 되는 것이에요.

❌ ③ routine(일과): 반복되는 습관적 절차예요.

❌ ④ bargain(흥정, 싼 물건): 거래와 관련된 말이에요.
det.tip: framework: (판단·사고의) 틀, 뼈대

questions.passage: We are all __________ (bias) by our personal history. Our ingrained beliefs are the result of our personal experiences in the past, and they shape our visual prism.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: We are all __________ (bias) by our personal history.

→ be동사 are 뒤 + by(~에 의해)가 이어지는 수동태 구조예요.
→ '우리는 개인적 이력에 의해 편향되어 있다'이므로 bias를 과거분사 biased로 바꿔요.

따라서 정답은 biased예요.
det.tip: be biased by ~: ~에 의해 편향되다 (수동태 be + p.p.)

questions.passage: You likely also grossly overestimate the chance of those events happening again. Morgan Housel offers a helpful __________ (suggest) to help us better empathize.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: Morgan Housel offers a helpful __________ (suggest).

→ 관사 a와 형용사 helpful의 꾸밈을 받는 명사 자리예요.
→ 동사 suggest(제안하다)를 명사 suggestion(제안)으로 바꿔요. offers a helpful suggestion = 도움이 되는 제안을 내놓다.

따라서 정답은 suggestion이에요.
det.tip: suggest(동사: 제안하다) → suggestion(명사: 제안)

questions.passage: We are all biased by our personal history. Our ingrained beliefs are the result of our personal experiences in the past, and they shape our visual prism. If you were born in a poor family or have been discriminated against, you already believe in something that people who have not experienced those things never will. You likely also grossly overestimate the chance of those events happening again. Morgan Housel offers a helpful suggestion to help us better empathize: “Start with the assumption that everyone is innocently out of touch and you’ll be more likely to explore what’s going on through __________, instead of cramming what’s going on into the framework of your own experiences. It’s hard to do. It’s uncomfortable when you do. But it’s the only way to get closer to figuring out why people behave like they do.”
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ④ multiple points of view(다양한 관점): 자기 경험의 틀에 상황을 욱여넣는 것(instead of ~)과 대비되는 바람직한 방식이므로 '다양한 관점을 통해' 탐색한다가 맞아요.

❌ ① a single fixed lens(하나의 고정된 렌즈): 글이 경계하는 방식이에요.

❌ ② your own past memories(자신의 과거 기억): 자기 경험의 틀과 같은 방향이라 instead of와 모순이에요.

❌ ③ the eyes of famous experts(유명 전문가의 시각): 본문에 없는 내용이에요.
det.tip: through multiple points of view: 다양한 관점을 통해

questions.passage: We are all biased by our personal history. Our ingrained beliefs are the result of our personal experiences in the past, and they shape our visual prism. If you were born in a poor family or have been discriminated against, you already believe in something that people who have not experienced those things never will. You likely also grossly overestimate the chance of those events happening again. Morgan Housel offers a helpful suggestion to help us better empathize: “Start with the assumption that everyone is innocently out of touch and you’ll be more likely to explore what’s going on through multiple points of view, instead of cramming what’s going on into __________. It’s hard to do. It’s uncomfortable when you do. But it’s the only way to get closer to figuring out why people behave like they do.”
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸: the framework of your own experiences(자기 경험의 틀)
det.analysis:
✅ ③ the framework of your own experiences(자기 경험의 틀): cramming what’s going on into ~(상황을 ~에 욱여넣기)는 다양한 관점 탐색의 나쁜 대안이므로, '자기 자신의 경험이라는 틀'이 들어가야 해요. 글 전체의 주제(개인사에 의한 편향)와도 일치해요.

❌ ① the opinions of unbiased outsiders(편향 없는 외부인의 의견): '욱여넣기'의 대상으로 부정적 맥락에 맞지 않아요.

❌ ② a brand-new set of shared beliefs(새로운 공동의 믿음): 본문에 없는 내용이에요.

❌ ④ the suggestions of professional writers(전문 작가들의 제안): Housel이 작가라는 점을 이용한 함정으로, 빈칸 맥락과 무관해요.
det.tip: cram A into B: A를 B에 욱여넣다 — B 자리에는 글이 경계하는 '자기 경험의 틀'
